walkthroughs.body_html:
A magnet is an object that can attract certain materials, especially iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

Every magnet has two ends called poles: north (N) and south (S).

The basic rule: opposite poles attract, like poles repel.

Only some materials are magnetic:

Iron, steel, nickel, cobalt - YES.
Wood, plastic, gold, aluminium - NO.

That's why a fridge magnet sticks to the door (steel) but not to a wooden cupboard.

A magnetic material can be magnetised if you stroke it repeatedly with a magnet.

A magnet's force fills a region called its magnetic field.

We draw field lines with arrows:

Lines go out of the north pole, curve around, and into the south pole.

Closer lines = stronger field. Near a pole, lines are packed - that's where forces are strongest.
